Baseband Catalog v1 - Data Release

Described in CHIME/FRB Coll. et al. 2024

The beamformed files in the data release are in the `beamformed_files` directory.
They are in the HDF5 format and can be read into Python with the `h5py` module.
The structure of each file is as follows. A quick description is reported for important groups.

    first_packet_recv_time
    history
    index_map
        amplitude_norm : Normalization factor to rescale the signal amplitude in each channel to a flux density (Jy)
        beam
        downsampled_time
        freq : Center frequency values (MHz) of each channel and their index
        input
        time
    reverse_map
    tiedbeam_baseband : Array of beamformed channelized voltages with shape (frequency, polarization, time)
    tiedbeam_locations : Center of the beam (ATTENTION, this does not consider a rotation of the telescope around the vertical axis that is corrected for in the source position)
    tiedbeam_power : Array of signal intensity with shape (frequency, polarization, time) coherently dedispersed to the value reported in the group attributes.
    time0 : Time of the beginning of each channel, in units of 2.56us-frames since the last telescope start and in Unix time. The precision is also reported.
    
The HDF5 object and all of the groups have attributes that provide additional metadata. They can be accessed with the `attrs` method.

An example to load one of the beamformed HDF5 files and to produce a waterfall plot is reported in `Example_make_waterfall.py`.
Note that this is a simplified version of the code used to process baseband data in the cataog and results will be slightly different.

An example to reproduce the polarization plots showed in Pandhi, A. et al. 2024 is reported in `Example_polarization_script.py`. Diagnostic plots for the polarization results are stored in the folder named `polarization_plots`.
